findings.claim: The isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), which reduces to owner-only. A team ADMIN who is neither organizer nor attendee gets FORBIDDEN, and the variable name no longer matches what the check computes.
findings.evidence: isTeamAdmin (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284) matches ADMIN or OWNER; isTeamOwner (:286-295) matches OWNER only. The repo convention is role === OWNER || role === ADMIN (confirm.handler.ts:127-128, get.handler.ts:405-406). Repro: a team ADMIN, not organizer or attendee, calls viewer.bookings.addGuests and gets FORBIDDEN. Reasoned; not executed.
findings.reason: Four seats agree and give a concrete repro. Write that repro as a failing handler test before fixing. The fix is isTeamAdmin alone, which also drops one DB query. The mattpocock Mysterious Name point (finding 12) is the same root cause and is merged here.

findings.claim: The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS filter compares the raw guest email against a lowercased blacklist, so changing the case (e.g. Bad@x.com) bypasses it.
findings.evidence: The blacklist is lowercased but the check is .includes(guest) on the unlowercased input. handleNewBooking.ts:741-745 and checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts:17-18 lowercase before comparing. Repro: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=bad@x.com with guests:["Bad@x.com"] inserts and emails the address. Reasoned; not executed.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Make the mixed-case repro a failing test before fixing.

findings.claim: The blacklist filter never applies extractBaseEmail, so a plus-alias (bad+1@x.com) bypasses it.
findings.evidence: There is no extractBaseEmail call before the blacklist comparison. The repo convention is extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() (handleNewBooking.ts:741-743). Repro: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=bad@x.com with guests:["bad+1@x.com"] is inserted and emailed. Reasoned; not executed.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. This is a separate cause from the case-sensitivity finding. Make the plus-alias repro a failing test before fixing.

findings.claim: The de-duplication against existing attendees is case-sensitive, so A@x.com is added as a new attendee next to an existing a@x.com.
findings.evidence: The existing-attendee comparison on handler lines 74-78 uses raw string equality.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Normalised to Minor because the impact is a duplicate attendee row and email, not a security or data-loss issue.

findings.claim: The handler passes the raw guests input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests. An already-existing attendee who is re-submitted gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' update.
findings.evidence: email-manager.ts:541-545 sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to every attendee whose email is in newGuests.

findings.claim: The server does not de-duplicate emails within one request. Only the client dialog refine does. A direct tRPC call with ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] creates two attendee rows and sends two emails.
findings.evidence: ZAddGuestsInputSchema has no uniqueness refine. The client check lives in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-30. Inserts go through createMany.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Add a server-side uniqueness check.

findings.claim: The server never checks booking status or time. Guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, which writes attendee rows and sends REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS invites for a dead booking.
findings.evidence: There is no status or endTime check in the handler. The UI gates the action (BookingListItem.tsx:544), but the API accepts any booking id. The ICS method and status are set in attendee-add-guests-email.ts:10-17 and organizer-add-guests-email.ts:14-20. Reasoned; not executed.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Make a cancelled-booking addGuests test red before fixing.

findings.claim: On seated events (seatsPerTimeSlot), guests are added as Attendee rows with no BookingSeat records, which bypasses the seat model and the seat limit.
findings.evidence: The handler has no seatsPerTimeSlot branch and creates attendees directly. Reasoned; not executed.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Normalised to Important because it bypasses a capacity limit. Needs a red test on a seated booking before fixing.

findings.claim: The onError fallback `${code}: ${t(msg)}` || t("unable_to_add_guests") can never fall through, so the unable_to_add_guests key is dead and users see raw strings like BAD_REQUEST: ....
findings.evidence: A template string with literal ': ' is never falsy.

findings.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail settings, and the handler passes no metadata.
findings.evidence: Sibling senders gate on these settings: sendLocationChangeEmails at email-manager.ts:495-523 and sendScheduledSeatsEmails at 248/260. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. Not fixed this round.

findings.claim: The guests array has no .max() size cap, so one request can mail any number of addresses in the organizer's name.
findings.evidence: The schema has no length limit. Emails go out from organizer.name with replyTo organizer.email. Reasoned.

findings.claim: The authorization is wider than the sibling editLocation: plain authedProcedure lets any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee add guests.
findings.evidence: editLocation uses bookingsProcedure (bookings/util.ts:19-63), which allows only the organizer or a COLLECTIVE host. The route is at _router.tsx:79. Reasoned. mattpocock notes there is no spec to say which model is intended.

findings.claim: Collective co-hosts who are neither booking.userId nor attendees are refused, which is a regression against bookingsProcedure.
findings.evidence: The custom check covers organizer, attendee and team owner only. bookingsProcedure in util.ts allows COLLECTIVE hosts.

findings.claim: AttendeeScheduledEmail is constructed without showAttendees, so seated events with seatsShowAttendees=true show only the recipient in add-guests emails.
findings.evidence: The constructor is at attendee-scheduled-email.ts:19-26. The email class is attendee-add-guests-email.ts.

findings.claim: sendAddGuestsEmails emails every attendee the full attendee list regardless of seatsShowAttendees.
findings.evidence: Reasoned by mattpocock (finding 9).
findings.reason: Disproved by the open-code-review and superpowers reports. Both cite attendee-scheduled-email.ts:19-26: with showAttendees unset, seated-event emails list only the recipient. So attendee emails hide the list rather than leak it.

findings.claim: On seated events, the full attendee list is pushed to the organizer's calendar event, which can expose seat-holders to each other through the provider invite even when seatsShowAttendees is false.
findings.evidence: updateCalendarAttendees is called with all attendees. Reasoned. The seat did not verify how Google notifies invitees.

findings.claim: evt is built without team, so the team-member loop in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs and team hosts are never notified.
findings.evidence: email-manager.ts:531-537 iterates calendarEvent.team?.members.

findings.claim: EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials, not the organizer's. References without a credentialId, and CRM refs, are matched against the caller's credentials, so the organizer's event can be skipped or updated with the wrong credential.
findings.evidence: See EventManager.ts:872-878. booking.user.credentials is fetched but unused. open-code-review considered this and chose not to report it because of the credentialId DB fallback. That does not cover refs lacking a credentialId.

findings.claim: The booking include loads user.credentials (full credential keys) that are never read.
findings.evidence: The credentials actually used come from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) at line 160. The block is copied from util.ts:48-58.

findings.claim: The findFirst uses include: {...: true}, which triggers the repo lint rule @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true (warn).
findings.evidence: See the packages/eslint-plugin recommended rules. The precedent copy in bookingsProcedure has the same warning.

findings.claim: MultiEmail is a near-verbatim copy of the multiemail factory in packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:231-310, which is left in place, so two copies will drift.
findings.evidence: The original carries the comment //TODO: Make it a ui component. The copies already differ in data-testid, htmlFor and array mutation.
findings.reason: Appendix: two advisory seats. Normalised from ponytail's Important to Minor: duplication, not a defect.

findings.claim: updateCalendarAttendees runs after the attendee insert with no try/catch or transaction. If it throws, the guests are saved but the client gets an error and no emails go out, and a retry fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid.
findings.evidence: Insert at lines 91-104, calendar call at about line 165, no compensation. Reasoned.

findings.claim: The email-send catch logs a fixed string and drops err.
findings.evidence: The catch block in handler lines 165-171.

findings.claim: There is no transaction or uniqueness guard, so two concurrent requests can both pass the de-dup and insert the same guest.
findings.evidence: Check-then-createMany with no lock. Reasoned.

findings.claim: The handler throws you_do_not_have_permission, which is not in en/common.json, so the user sees the raw key.
findings.evidence: Reported by open-code-review against AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-46.

findings.claim: isInvalidEmail is not cleared after a successful add or on edit, so a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error can show.
findings.evidence: State is reset only by the Cancel button.

findings.claim: Closing via onOpenChange (overlay or Esc) keeps the old email values and error state when the dialog is reopened.
findings.evidence: onOpenChange does not reset state.

findings.claim: If every email field is removed, handleAdd returns with no feedback.
findings.evidence: Early return in handleAdd.

findings.claim: The client-side uniqueness refine is case-sensitive.
findings.evidence: The refine compares raw strings.

findings.claim: The Zod validation schema is rebuilt on every render inside the component body.
findings.evidence: The schema and refine are defined in the component body.

findings.claim: New guests are saved with name "", so emails and calendar entries show blank names. They also silently inherit the organizer's time zone and locale.
findings.evidence: Attendee createMany data at handler lines 83-88.

findings.claim: A new authenticated mutation that writes to the DB, calls calendars and sends email ships with zero tests: no handler integration test and no E2E test for the dialog.
findings.evidence: The patch adds no test files. mattpocock notes CONTRIBUTING.md does not require tests, but that does not disprove the risk claim.

findings.claim: data-testid="add_members" is added but nothing uses it.
findings.evidence: No test references it.

findings.claim: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow re-fetches the organizer that booking.user already loaded.
findings.evidence: include user at lines 36-41. The same habit exists in editLocation.handler.ts:32.

findings.claim: credentials: [...credentials] copies the array for no reason.
findings.evidence: The array is never mutated.

findings.claim: About 40 lines of event-building (attendee translation map, evt, destination-calendar ternary) are copied from editLocation.handler.ts:57-95.
findings.evidence: The blocks are near-identical; only location and conferenceCredentialId differ.

findings.claim: The lazy wrapper is unnecessary, and its '40kb' comment, copied from PhoneInputLazy and AddressInputLazy, is untrue here. MultiEmail uses only components @calcom/ui already ships.
findings.evidence: MultiEmail imports only EmailField, Button, Icon and Tooltip.

coverage: No files skipped: all four seats reviewed all 15 patch files. superpowers and open-code-review only skimmed common.json, packages/ui/index.tsx, MultiEmailLazy.tsx and the email template wrappers and index. The gate was not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored: no lint, typecheck, build or tests ran, and every finding is reasoned, with none executed. No spec, so the spec axis uses only intent implied by the patch. Standards sources were limited to CONTRIBUTING.md, packages/config/eslint-preset.js, packages/eslint-plugin rules and sibling-code conventions. Not checked: recurring-booking behaviour (only one occurrence updated); whether updateAllCalendarEvents swallows provider errors; how Google Calendar notifies invitees in the seated case; and non-en locales (Crowdin-managed). No reviewer from another model family held a correctness seat. Step-4 verdicts only: no fixes applied and no re-review rounds.
